findings.note: The Resolver iterates affected_components in dependency-provided order instead of explicitly sorting component IDs. This violates REQ-005's input-order invariance and T-003's required ascending-lexicographic evaluation order, making evaluation records and subprocess order dependent on upstream array ordering.

A WARN Block emits only one severity:block summary diagnostic. REQ-004 and AC-056 require one distinct severity:warn diagnostic per encountered WARN evidence node plus exactly one severity:block summary; the implementation neither retains WARN-node locations nor emits those required entries.

Blocks reached after Registry discovery/evaluation write a minimal Evidence object containing evaluations and diagnostics but omit the already-known context_binding and resolver provenance. TEST-012 and the step-9 design require a full Resolver Evidence record for these post-discovery Blocks; the supplied passing block tests therefore validate an under-specified oracle.
The wrappers emit check-id runtime-unavailable and exit 3, outside the Resolver's closed sixteen-value diagnostic enum and fixed 0/1/2 exit-code contract.
